name: tokenfuse
description: TokenFuse — runtime control for AI agents: per-run budgets, loop detection, burn forecast, kill-switch. Observability shows the fire; TokenFuse is the automatic extinguisher.

paragraphs: The runtime kill-switch for AI agents: cap their spend, stop runaway loops before they bill you.
A proxy you drop in front of every LLM call - it also blocks poisoned MCP tools and keeps secrets out of the model.
The kill-switch isn't a dashboard button you press after the fact - it's an HTTP 402 the gateway returns mid-run, before the provider bills you.

whatItDoes.text: The runtime kill-switch for AI agents: cap their spend, stop runaway loops before they bill you.

requirements.text: > ⚡ Try it in one command, no signup, no account: > bash > docker run -p 4100:4100 -e TOKENFUSEALLOWSTUB=1 ghcr.io/taipanbox/tokenfuse:v1.18.0 > > TOKENFUSEALLOWSTUB=1 is what makes this offline: with no provider behind > it, the gateway answers from a built-in stub and meters a fixed 1000/500 > tokens, so every figure it shows you is invented.
Put the provider key in a file and point TOKENFUSEUPSTREAMKEYFILE at it: TokenFuse then sends the key upstream itself, and your agents need only a TokenFuse key, never the provider's.

MCP servers are a new, live attack surface: a client typically re-fetches tools/list on every connection and trusts whatever comes back, so a tool a human already approved can silently change behavior later, without anyone re-reviewing it. tokenfuse mcp-scan is a free, standalone CLI - no TokenFuse account, gateway, or Cloud connection required.
Gate it in CI with the repo's own composite GitHub Action - no self-hosted scanning infra:
Platform / DevOps teams who need guardrails and cost visibility across many agents.

TokenFuse is open source (Apache-2.0) and free to self-host, with no seat limits and no time limit: the CLI, the local proxy, tokenfuse mcp-scan and its GitHub Action, and the Cloud control plane and dashboard (fleet spend, alerts, central budgets, the kill-switch).
